Package io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava

Class TopicRegistry

java.lang.Object
io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava.TopicRegistry
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class TopicRegistry extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A live, self-updating view of the topics visible on a Zenoh network.

Merges every available discovery channel into one keyed set. See TopicSource for what each channel proves. Two channels feed this registry:

  • An INTEREST sent to the router, which replays the current declarations (subscribers, queryables, liveliness tokens) and then streams changes as they happen.
  • Optionally a wildcard subscription, which records the key of every message that actually arrives.

Obtain one from PureJavaZenohSubscriber.topics(String, boolean), read it with snapshot() whenever you want the current picture, and close() it when finished. The pull API deliberately mirrors PureJavaZenohScout.snapshot(), which solves the same shape of problem for router discovery.

Live versus cumulative

A registry is one of two things, fixed at construction:

  • Live (the default): a picture of what exists right now. A topic drops out of the snapshot once every declaration behind it is withdrawn.
  • Cumulative: an accumulating record of everything seen since the registry started. Nothing is ever removed. A topic that has gone away is still reported, with TopicInfo.active() false and TopicInfo.activeSources() empty. This is the mode behind PureJavaZenohSubscriber.recordedTopics().

Observed traffic is sticky in both modes. Once a message has been seen on a key, that key stays in the snapshot, because a message really having arrived is not something a later event can retract.

What this is not

This is not an authoritative topic list, because Zenoh does not have one. It is the union of what several imperfect channels could see. A topic absent from a snapshot may still exist. Treat the result as a lower bound, never as proof of absence.

Threading

Safe from any thread. Updates arrive on the session reader thread; snapshot() may be called concurrently from anywhere and never blocks the reader.

  • Method Details

    • snapshot

      public List<TopicInfo> snapshot()
      An immutable snapshot of everything known, sorted by key expression.

      In a live registry every entry is active. In a cumulative one the result also includes topics that have since gone away, flagged with TopicInfo.active() false; filter with activeOnly() if you only want what is there now.

      Never blocks and never throws. Calling it before awaitCurrent(Duration) returns is legal and simply yields a partial picture.

    • activeOnly

      public List<TopicInfo> activeOnly()
      snapshot() filtered to topics whose evidence still stands.

      On a live registry this is the same as snapshot(), since nothing inactive is retained there.

    • isCumulative

      public boolean isCumulative()
      True if this registry accumulates rather than tracking live state, so a topic once seen is reported for the rest of the run.

    • awaitCurrent

      public boolean awaitCurrent(Duration timeout) throws InterruptedException
      Block until the router finishes replaying current declarations, or the timeout expires.

      This covers the declaration channel only. Observed traffic has no completion signal by nature, since there is no way to know a silent topic will stay silent, so a caller wanting traffic must simply wait as long as it is willing to.

      Returns:
      true if the replay completed, false on timeout
      Throws:
      InterruptedException

    • close

      public void close()
      Stop discovery. Sends a FINAL INTEREST and closes the traffic subscription if one was opened. Idempotent. Any snapshot already taken remains valid, and snapshot() keeps working after close, simply frozen at the last known state.
